body: Authenticated summary reads now negotiate bounded fast gzip in the existing blocking workers, retaining identity compatibility, no-store and source/credential/command boundaries. In five quiet release samples at 1,000 cards, desktop Calendar JSON falls from 344 to 75 KB (78%); constrained warm readiness falls from 1,478.9 to 1,080.5 ms (27%) with the same 995 dated items and 7,338 DOM elements. Local Unix response encoding adds about 0.26 ms median over 200 alternating samples per encoding. Focus gains only about 19 ms warm. Full gate: 249 Rust, 112 JavaScript and 12 Python tests. All 20 Chromium suites, six affected WebKit suites and broad HTTPS pass. The rebuilt/restarted manual app preserves 27 existing resource versions, two pins, preferences and certificate; HTTPS assets and live compression are verified. Pinned Rust dependencies pass the current advisory/license check and their release notices are included. Evidence and protocol: progress/2026-09-30-deep-performance.md and ADR-052. Emulation is not physical-device/VPN acceptance. Calendar rendering and the durable-write target remain open; no scope or card status changes.

metadata.summary: Bounded gzip reduces large Calendar transfer and loading time
